sections.title: Objective type questions: each has two parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Define aptitude.
questions.answer: A combination of characteristics indicating an individual's capacity to acquire specific knowledge or skill after learning.

questions.q: Name two specialised aptitude tests.
questions.answer: Mechanical Aptitude Test and Musical Aptitude Test.

questions.q: Name two multiple aptitude test batteries.
questions.answer: Differential Aptitude Tests (DAT) and General Aptitude Test Battery (GATB).

questions.q: Define interest.
questions.answer: A tendency to choose one activity in preference to another or to seek out an activity or object.

questions.q: Name the two types of interest.
questions.answer: Intrinsic interest and extrinsic interest.

questions.q: Name two interest inventories.
questions.answer: Strong Vocational Interest Blank (SVIB) and Kuder Preference Record.

questions.q: Define IQ and give its formula.
questions.answer: IQ is the ratio of mental age to chronological age multiplied by 100: IQ = MA/CA x 100.

questions.q: Calculate the IQ of a child with MA 9 and CA 12.
Why is IQ not meaningful beyond 18 years?
questions.answer: Mental ability is usually fully developed by then, so the concept of mental age does not apply.

sections.title: Objective type questions: each has four parts of 1 mark.

questions.q: Calculate the IQ: (i) MA 10, CA 8; (ii) MA 12, CA 12; (iii) MA 6, CA 8; (iv) classify each as above, average or below average.
questions.answer: (i) 125 (above average). (ii) 100 (average). (iii) 75 (below average). (iv) as stated.

questions.q: Identify intrinsic or extrinsic interest: (i) painting for pure enjoyment; (ii) studying only for a prize; (iii) playing for a salary; (iv) reading with no reward.
questions.answer: (i) Intrinsic. (ii) Extrinsic. (iii) Extrinsic. (iv) Intrinsic.

questions.q: Name the techniques of measuring interest (four).
questions.answer: Self-ratings, interviews, questionnaires, checklists and inventories (any four).

questions.q: What does a job description give? Name four items.
questions.answer: Nature of work, salary and benefits, work timings and holidays, required intelligence, aptitude and interest (any four).

sections.title: Very short answer questions. Answer in 30–50 words.

questions.q: What three things does aptitude involve?
questions.answer: Readiness to acquire a skill, ability to acquire it and ability to derive satisfaction from the activity.

questions.q: How is intrinsic interest different from extrinsic interest?
questions.answer: Intrinsic interest is pleasure in the activity itself; extrinsic is pleasure from reward, praise or money.

questions.q: Why are interest inventories better than interviews?
questions.answer: They use many specific questions covering a broad range of careers or subjects.

questions.q: What is ability?
questions.answer: The innate capacity to act that helps in solving a problem; environment can develop it but cannot produce it.

questions.q: What is mental age?
questions.answer: The age level of questions a child can answer correctly, as most children of that age can.

questions.q: What is the use of aptitude tests?
questions.answer: They help in educational and vocational guidance by predicting probable success with training.

questions.q: What is the purpose of a job description?
questions.answer: To inform applicants about the nature of work, pay and conditions and the aptitude, interest and ability required, attracting the right people.

sections.title: Short answer questions. Answer in 50–80 words.

questions.q: Explain the concept of aptitude.
questions.answer: Aptitude is a special potential in a field, resulting from heredity and environment; it needs readiness, ability and satisfaction, predicts success with training and can be enhanced and assessed.

questions.q: Describe the types of aptitude tests.
questions.answer: Specialised tests such as the Mechanical and Musical Aptitude Tests; general aptitude tests; and multiple aptitude batteries such as DAT and GATB measuring several separate areas.

questions.q: Distinguish intrinsic and extrinsic interests with examples.
questions.answer: Intrinsic: liking painting for itself; extrinsic: doing a task for money or praise. Intrinsic interest gives a better job match.

questions.q: Explain mental age and IQ.
questions.answer: Mental age is age-related mental maturity from age scales; IQ = MA/CA x 100. IQ 100 is average, above 100 above average; not meaningful after 18, so profiles of abilities are used.

questions.q: Explain the role of aptitude, interest and ability in career choice.
questions.answer: Career choices should match all three; a right decision brings happiness and job satisfaction, using accurate information about the job and the person.

questions.q: Explain what a job description contains.
questions.answer: Nature of work, salary and benefits, timings and holidays and the intelligence, aptitude and interest required, e.g. a teacher needs communication skills, patience and qualifications.

sections.title: Long answer questions. Answer in 80–120 words.

questions.q: What is aptitude? Describe one aptitude test and its use.
questions.answer: Aptitude is the capacity to acquire a skill with training from heredity and environment. The Differential Aptitude Tests (DAT) are a battery measuring several separate areas and are used in educational and vocational guidance to predict future performance.

questions.q: What is interest? How does it help in the choice of subjects and careers?
questions.answer: Interest is a preference for an activity, intrinsic or extrinsic, measured by self-ratings, interviews, questionnaires and inventories such as SVIB and Kuder. Inventory results guide selection of streams, courses and careers when supplemented by ability and aptitude tests.

questions.q: Discuss ability and intelligence, mental age and IQ.
questions.answer: Ability is the innate capacity to act; intelligence is its important form; Gardner holds there are multiple intelligences. Mental age comes from age scales and IQ = MA/CA x 100, with 100 average; not meaningful after 18, so ability profiles are used.

questions.q: Describe the role of aptitudes, interests and abilities in educational and vocational choices and the importance of job descriptions.
questions.answer: The three together guide choice of study, hobbies and careers; the right decision gives satisfaction. Job descriptions give nature of work, pay and conditions and the required aptitude, interest and ability to attract suitable applicants.
